newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin regrets Duma delay on chemical arms treaty.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin regrets Duma delay on chemical arms treaty.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin expressed regret on Tuesday that parliament had failed to ratify an international treaty banning chemical weapons before it came into force, Itar-Tass news agency reported.
Presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky told Tass Yeltsin had voiced his concern in the Black Sea resort of Sochi where he is on holiday.
The State Duma, or lower house of parliament, discussed the treaty on Friday but said it would not ratify it immediately even though it was due to come into effect on Tuesday.

"Russian President Boris Yeltsin expresses his regret that 'a radical part of the State Duma, having wasted time on various resolutions which have no legal force and show signs of various kinds of phobias, did not examine one of the main disarmament questions in time,'" Tass said.
"This has put Russia in a more than delicate situation," he quoted Yeltsin as saying.

The failure to ratify the treaty was the latest problem between Yeltsin and the communist-led Duma, which has opposed him and the government on several recent legislative issues and has been told by the president to improve its work.
The Duma ignored international pressure to ratify the treaty, even though the United States Senate approved it last Thursday and it has been signed by 164 countries.
The European Union urged Russia, which has huge stockpiles of chemical weapons, to follow the U.S. lead. Britain and France also issued individual appeals.
But the Duma decided simply to send a statement to the other participating countries saying they would try to ratify it in a few months' time.
The deputies also backed a draft law laying down how, but not when, Russia would destroy the weapons.
